{{Short description|Two collections of integer sequences with no such sequence lying between them}}

{{inline|date=December 2022}}
In [[mathematics]], a '''Hausdorff gap''' consists roughly of two collections of sequences of [[natural number]]s, such that there is no sequence lying between the two collections. The first example was found by {{harvs|txt|last=Hausdorff|authorlink=Felix Hausdorff|year=1909}}. The existence of Hausdorff gaps shows that the [[partially ordered set]] of possible growth rates of sequences is not [[complete partial order|complete]].

==Definition==

Let <math>\omega^\omega</math> be the set of all sequences of non-negative integers, and define <math>f<g</math> to mean <math>\lim \left (g(n)-f(n)\right )=+\infty</math>.

If <math>X</math> is a partially ordered set (poset) and <math>\kappa</math> and <math>\lambda</math> are [[cardinal number|cardinals]], then a <math>(\kappa,\lambda)</math>-''pregap'' in <math>X</math> is a set of elements <math>f_\alpha</math> for <math>\alpha\in\kappa</math> and a set of elements <math>g_\beta</math> for <math>\beta\in\lambda</math> such that:
*The transfinite sequence <math>f</math> is strictly increasing;
*The transfinite sequence <math>g</math> is strictly decreasing;
*Every element of the sequence <math>f</math> is less than every element of the sequence <math>g</math>.

A pregap is called a ''gap'' if it satisfies the additional condition:

*There is no element <math>h</math> greater than all elements of <math>f</math> and less than all elements of <math>g</math>.

A '''Hausdorff gap''' is a <math>(\omega_1,\omega_1)</math>-gap in <math>\omega^\omega</math> such that for every [[countable ordinal]] <math>\alpha</math> (i.e. every <math>\alpha \in \omega_1</math>) and every natural number <math>n</math> there are only a finite number of <math>\beta</math> less than <math>\alpha</math> such that for all <math>k>n</math> we have <math>f_\alpha(k)<g_\beta(k)</math>.

There are some variations of these definitions, with the ordered set <math>\omega^\omega</math> replaced by a similar set. For example, one can redefine <math>f<g</math> to mean <math>f(n)<g(n)</math> for all but finitely many <math>n</math>. Another variation introduced by {{harvtxt|Hausdorff|1936}} is to replace <math>\omega^\omega</math> by the [[power set]] of <math>\omega</math>, with the order given by <math>A<B</math> if <math>A</math> has only finitely many elements not in <math>B</math> but <math>B</math> has infinitely many elements not in <math>A</math>.

==Existence==
It is possible to [[mathematical proof|prove]] in [[ZFC]] that there exist Hausdorff gaps and <math>(\mathfrak b,\omega)</math>-gaps where <math>\mathfrak b</math> is the [[cardinality]] of the smallest [[unbounded set]] in <math>\omega^\omega</math>, and that there are no <math>(\omega,\omega)</math>-gaps. The stronger [[open coloring axiom]] can rule out all types of gaps except Hausdorff gaps and those of type <math>(\kappa,\omega)</math> with <math>\kappa \geq \omega_2</math>.
